title: Projectivity lifts across a nilpotent ideal for a flat module
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq A$ a nilpotent ideal, and $M$ an $A$-module. If $M$ is flat over $A$ and $M/IM$ is projective over $A/I$, then $M$ is projective over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

proof.text: Choose $N\geq1$ with $I^N=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-projective-module-lift] to the projective $A/I$-module $M/IM$, obtaining a projective $A$-module $P$ and an $A/I$-linear isomorphism $\alpha:P/IP\xrightarrow{\sim}M/IM$. The lifting-along-surjections characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], applied to $M\twoheadrightarrow M/IM$ and the composite $P\to P/IP\xrightarrow{\alpha}M/IM$, gives an $A$-linear map $f:P\to M$ whose reduction is $\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], $P$ is flat; $M$ is flat by hypothesis. No finite generation is required for the lifting lemma or for the projective lifting property.

source.place: Tag 05CG, lemma-lift-projective, first three sentences; Tag 07LV, lemma-lift-projective-module; Tag 05CE, definition-projective

proof.text: For $X=P$ or $M$ and $0\leq a<N$, put $Q_a=I^a/I^{a+1}$. Tensor the inclusion $I^a\hookrightarrow A$ with $X$: [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact] makes $I^a\otimes_A X\to A\otimes_A X=X$ injective, and its image under multiplication is precisely $I^aX$, by the definition of ideal multiplication on a module. Thus multiplication identifies $I^a\otimes_A X$ with $I^aX$, also for $a+1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to $I^{a+1}\to I^a\to Q_a\to0$. Taking the cokernel under these multiplication identifications gives an isomorphism $Q_a\otimes_A X\xrightarrow{\sim}I^aX/I^{a+1}X$, sending $(r\bmod I^{a+1})\otimes x$ to $rx\bmod I^{a+1}X$. This is just the cited exact sequence with its first two terms identified; no additional flatness of $Q_a$ is asserted.

source.place: Tag 05CG, lemma-lift-projective, identification of the graded pieces; Tag 00HD, lemma-flat; Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact

proof.text: The module $Q_a$ is annihilated by $I$ since $I I^a\subseteq I^{a+1}$, so it is an $A/I$-module. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] identifies $Q_a\otimes_A X$ with $Q_a\otimes_{A/I}(X/IX)$. Combined with step 2 this sends $\bar r\otimes\bar x$ to $rx\bmod I^{a+1}X$. Under these explicit maps, the graded map induced by $f$ sends $rx$ to $rf(x)$, hence corresponds exactly to $1_{Q_a}\otimes\alpha$. It is invertible with inverse $1_{Q_a}\otimes\alpha^{-1}$: both composites are the identity on pure tensors, which generate the tensor product. Therefore every map $I^aP/I^{a+1}P\to I^aM/I^{a+1}M$ is bijective.

source.place: Tag 05CG, lemma-lift-projective, last displayed map and final sentence; Tag 051C, lemma-what-does-it-mean, quotient-ring tensor identification

proof.text: Prove by descending induction on $a=N,N-1,\ldots,0$ that $f_a:I^aP\to I^aM$ is bijective. For $a=N$ both modules are zero because $I^N=0$. Suppose $f_{a+1}$ is bijective. If $p\in I^aP$ and $f(p)=0$, injectivity on the $a$th graded piece implies $p\in I^{a+1}P$, and injectivity of $f_{a+1}$ gives $p=0$. For $m\in I^aM$, surjectivity on that graded piece supplies $p\in I^aP$ with $m-f(p)\in I^{a+1}M$. Surjectivity of $f_{a+1}$ supplies $p_1\in I^{a+1}P$ with $f(p_1)=m-f(p)$, so $f(p+p_1)=m$. This proves the induction step and therefore bijectivity of $f=f_0:P\to M$. Its inverse is $A$-linear, since uniqueness of preimages preserves addition and scalar multiplication.

source.place: Tag 05CG, lemma-lift-projective, finite filtrations and the reduction to their graded pieces

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-projective-direct-summand], clause (2), an $A$-module isomorphic to a projective $A$-module is projective. Apply it to $M\cong P$ from step 4 and the projective module $P$ from step 1. This proves the asserted projectivity of $M$.
